answer:
The paper uses a combination of different deep learning architectures for sign language recognition, applied to skeletal and RGB video data [1]. Specifically, it proposes an RNN architecture with a spatial data augmentation technique, and an architecture that uses both RGB and skeletal data to improve recognition accuracy [3]. The motivation for using RNNs is that sign recognition requires capturing temporal body motion, and RNNs can capture temporal dynamics by maintaining an internal state [8]. The paper also notes that it applied different deep learning architectures inspired by their success in computer vision [2].

In the literature it reviews, prior systems predominantly used RGB video data, with Hidden Markov Models to model sequential dependencies [3]; CNN with RGB video data has been shown effective for sign language recognition [6], and 3D CNNs have been used to extract spatio-temporal features from video [6].

Note: The context does not provide full architectural details (e.g., specific layer configurations) of the proposed models.
